chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Yahya al-Azraq from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was killed while he had a debt and left no wealth, so his family took the blood money (diyah) from his killer, is it upon them to pay off his debt? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And he left nothing?' He said, 'They only took the blood money, so it is upon them to pay off his debt.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation paid for killing
key_terms.قَضَاء: To pay off or settle (a debt)

ai.seo_question: How are a deceased person's debts handled if they leave no wealth but receive blood money?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that blood money (diyah) is considered part of the deceased's estate, thereby creating a financial obligation on the heirs to prioritize debt repayment from these funds. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the deceased's liabilities take precedence over the heirs' inheritance rights, ensuring creditors are satisfied before distribution. The hadith highlights the continuity of financial responsibility even after death, reinforcing the sanctity of fulfilling one's debts in Islamic law.
